audits.title: 848 Improving Compliance With Indwelling Catheter Securement in an Orthopedic Unit: A Two-Cycle Audit Against Best-Practice Standards
audits.standard: CDC and AHRQ CAUTI-prevention guidelines: securement device at insertion and throughout use; target ≥90% appropriate securement
audits.setting: Tertiary care orthopaedic unit (National Hospital of Sri Lanka)

cycle1.result: Only 10.4% had appropriately secured catheters (6.9% done intraoperatively, the rest in ICU); most ward-inserted catheters had no securement.

audits.intervention: Structured teaching for nursing and junior medical staff and a catheter care checklist with securement as a mandatory item.

cycle2.result: Appropriate securement improved to 40.7%, a near 4-fold increase but below the ≥90% benchmark.

audits.other_findings: Lack of staff awareness of the importance of securement was the main reason for poor practice.
audits.citation: Kankanamge G. Madhawa J, Peramuna S, Naligama A, Gnanasekeram R, Vinod Saranga K. 848 Improving Compliance With Indwelling Catheter Securement in an Orthopedic Unit: A Two-Cycle Audit Against Best-Practice Standards. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.252.

audits.title: STANDARDIZATION OF URINARY CATHETERIZATION GUIDELINES TO REDUCE PAEDIATRIC PERIOPERATIVE URINARY TRACT INFECTION RATES: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE
audits.standard: ACS NSQIP-Paediatric UTI rates; project aim of a 30% reduction in paediatric perioperative UTIs within 1 year
audits.setting: Tertiary care children's hospital, all paediatric surgical services

cycle1.result: Institution's paediatric UTI rate had an odds ratio of 1.9x compared with the predicted rate (NSQIP 'Needs Improvement'); audits of catheterisation practice identified areas for improvement.

audits.intervention: Multidisciplinary working group; 'permissive list' of procedures for which catheters may be required; standardised early catheter removal except urological procedures; education on insertion and maintenance; standardised equipment and technique; electronic medical record order sets as a forcing function.

cycle2.result: 47% reduction in perioperative UTI rate by project completion; 96% adherence to the 'permissive lists'; NSQIP-Paediatric status improved from 'Needs Improvement' to 'Exemplary'.

audits.other_findings: Implementation was delayed by COVID-19, giving a two-year project duration.
audits.citation: Charron B, Katchky R, Dann C, Orchard E, Lam J, Strychowsky J, et al.. STANDARDIZATION OF URINARY CATHETERIZATION GUIDELINES TO REDUCE PAEDIATRIC PERIOPERATIVE URINARY TRACT INFECTION RATES: A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE. Orthopaedic Proceedings. 2025;107-B(SUPP_13):150-150. doi:10.1302/1358-992x.2025.13.150.

audits.title: 133 Prospective Audit of Adherence to Current Guidelines for Urinary Catheterisation on a Dedicated Geriatric ward in a Tertiary Hospital
audits.standard: HSE guidelines on indications for urinary catheterisation
audits.setting: Dedicated geriatric ward, tertiary hospital (Beaumont Hospital, Dublin)

cycle1.result: Catheters inserted in 45.2% (n=14); insertion warranted per guidelines in only 42.85% (n=6).

audits.intervention: Ward-level and NCHD education recommended with re-audit.
audits.other_findings: Urinary incontinence (25.8%) was documented in admission notes in only 6.5%; healthcare associated infection in 6.5%.
audits.citation: Comber R. 133 Prospective Audit of Adherence to Current Guidelines for Urinary Catheterisation on a Dedicated Geriatric ward in a Tertiary Hospital. Age and Ageing. 2019;48(Supplement_3):iii17-iii65. doi:10.1093/ageing/afz103.78.

audits.title: Urinary catheterization in care homes for older people: self-reported questionnaire audit of catheter management by care home staff.
audits.standard: NICE and Association of Continence Care urinary catheter care standards
audits.setting: 37 randomly selected care homes for older people in three health districts, Gloucestershire

cycle1.result: 750/1438 (52%) staff responded; 83% of nursing and 40% of other care staff had formal catheter training; at least 10% did not wash hands before handling a catheter; bladder washouts used routinely by 50%; urine specimens taken from bag tap by 29% of nursing and 54% of other staff.

audits.other_findings: Compliance had improved greatly since a 1998 audit; only 45% of nursing and 40% of other staff encouraged residents to empty their own bags.
audits.citation: McNulty CA, Bowen J, Foy C, Gunn K, Freeman E, Tompkins D, et al.. Urinary catheterization in care homes for older people: self-reported questionnaire audit of catheter management by care home staff. J Hosp Infect. 2006;62(1):29-36. doi:10.1016/j.jhin.2005.03.008. PMID: 16309782.

audits.title: Urethral catheter audit.
audits.standard: Locally developed standards for urethral catheter care

cycle1.result: Catheter duration 1 to 38 days; in 13% duration could not be identified because of poor documentation.

audits.other_findings: Staff questionnaire (384 nurses, 174 doctors) showed low training levels and limited understanding; most nurses had never or rarely catheterised a child.
audits.citation: Bray L, Sanders C. Urethral catheter audit. Paediatr Nurs. 2007;19(3):14-16. doi:10.7748/paed.19.3.14.s19. PMID: 17472189.

audits.title: Clinical audit on indications and technique of male urethral catheterization in emergency department of a tertiary care hospital.
audits.standard: Lippincott guidelines and CDC hand hygiene guidelines for urethral catheterisation
audits.setting: Emergency department, Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi; tertiary care hospital

cycle1.result: Sterile technique maintained with sterile gloves and povidone-iodine, but hand hygiene not performed before the procedure 80% of the time.

audits.title: Audit of catheter management provided by District Nurses and Continence Advisors.
audits.standard: Previously formulated criteria grading management strategies A (best) to E (worst)
audits.setting: Postal survey of Welsh Continence Advisors and South Glamorgan District Nurses

cycle1.result: Continence Advisors had more A or B graded responses in all areas; with marked bacteriuria 60% of Continence Advisors but 11% of District Nurses would assess whether the patient was ill; 53% of District Nurses would give antibiotics without assessment.

audits.other_findings: Responses from all 10 Continence Advisors and 73/139 (53%) District Nurses; only one District Nurse considered constipation or detrusor spasm for suprapubic pain.
audits.citation: Capewell AE, Morris SL. Audit of catheter management provided by District Nurses and Continence Advisors. Br J Urol. 1993;71(3):259-264. doi:10.1111/j.1464-410x.1993.tb15939.x. PMID: 8477311.

audits.title: Trial removal of indwelling urinary catheters in stroke patients: a clinical audit at North Shore Hospital.
audits.standard: 2016 AHA/ASA guidelines on trial removal of catheter
audits.setting: Acute stroke ward, North Shore Hospital, Auckland

cycle1.result: 4.1% had catheter removed within 24 hours; mean about five catheter days; 24.5% developed UTI.

audits.other_findings: Insufficient documentation and inappropriate indications for catheter insertion; daily electronic reminders recommended.
audits.citation: Rasanathan D, Wang X. Trial removal of indwelling urinary catheters in stroke patients: a clinical audit at North Shore Hospital. N Z Med J. 2020;133(1512):15-21. PMID: 32242174.

audits.title: [A quality improvement project on urinary catheter management in a medical ward of the Turin local health authority].
audits.standard: Institutional recommendations on urinary catheter management
audits.setting: Medical ward, Ospedale Maria Vittoria, ASL Città di Torino

cycle1.result: Baseline: documentation of catheter indication 59.2%; daily reassessment 25%; catheter size documented 46.1%; 76 catheterisations; median duration 8 days; CAUTI 20 per 1,000 catheter-days.

audits.intervention: Two PDSA cycles: audit-feedback, multiprofessional briefings, training, electronic reminders, support materials, project champion, self-assessment questionnaire.

cycle2.result: After PDSA2: indication documented 94.8%; daily reassessment 89.6%; size documented 98.3%; 58 catheterisations; median 6 days; CAUTI 13.77 per 1,000 catheter-days (not significant).

audits.citation: De Prospo T, Labita S, Melis G, Scolari L, Viottini E, Del Colle S, et al.. [A quality improvement project on urinary catheter management in a medical ward of the Turin local health authority]. Assist Inferm Ric. 2026;45(3):135-145. doi:10.1702/4774.47962. PMID: 42765959.
